answer.evidence: The chair faces north, so the view is of its back. Rows 2-4 are the post tops, with a narrow gap between them at the top (width 4 at row 2, 8 at row 3, 10 at row 4). Rows 4-13 are a constant 10 wide and read as vertical slats. Light bands at rows 7 and 9 alternate with darker gaps at rows 6, 10-11 and 13. No band ends in a front-edge line with eave shadow, no ellipse forms, and no contents are visible. The seat surface is not seen from above; it is hidden behind the backrest. Rows 14-15 are narrow legs (width 6, then 4). This matches the red 'seat: band 2' and 'front elevation' references, not the green seat with a 5-row top.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny chair, about 16x20 source pixels, with only 7 distinct colours. The references have 14 colours (bench, lamp) up to 38-40 (well, stall). 78% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline reads as a dark grey/black line around the whole shape. The bench reference is 44% neutral and carries tinted dark browns. By eye the chair has about 3 wood steps: a light plank, a mid tone and a dark outline. There is no visible grain, no per-plank highlight and no wood texture. The bench has about 5 wood steps, with plank highlights and shadowed legs. The per-tile median of 0 is not held against the chair because it is a small prop. Even judged by eye, it is flatter and more sticker-like than the bench, with half its colours. Flat-fill coverage is 0% only because the piece is small. The shading is shallow and the outline is the uniform dark line Beodeul avoids, so it fails.
